intro: Monday June 22. First full US session post-3-day closure. The long-term thesis continues to strengthen through the post-FOMC turbulence. June 22 developments that reinforce the structural picture: (1) NVDA's 50-DMA at ~$206.74 held as intraday support (session low $206.50) with 241M shares of institutional volume — confirming the June 18 50-DMA recovery was structural, not a false break; (2) Micron Q3 consensus has been revised UP again to revenue $34.66B / EPS $19.95 / gross margin >80% (27 analysts Strong Buy, HBM sold-out through 2026-2027) — the structural AI memory demand signal is now stronger than at any point in Micron's history, directly validating the NVDA and SK Hynix long theses; (3) SK Hynix ADR process confirmed proceeding normally (Seoul Economic Daily June 22 article) — SEC clearance expected late June, Nasdaq listing July–August 2026, $66B total shareholder return ($14B ADR + buyback); (4) SPCX IG ratings being priced in at ~$185 (from $174.90 June 18 stop close) — the Moody's Baa1 / Fitch BBB+ / S&P BBB franchise quality floor is permanent regardless of near-term price action; (5) BTC double-bottom ($62,255–$62,313) intact through Day 2 of the second stop-clock event — structural floor holds. The AI infrastructure supercycle driven by AI semis, AI memory, big-tech AI monetization, space infrastructure, and Bitcoin's fixed-supply adoption ramp has not been altered by Warsh's hawkish FOMC or the post-FOMC Week 2 caution on June 22. The post-FOMC discount at current levels is the structural accumulation opportunity for investors with 1–4 year horizons.

ideas.name: NVIDIA
ideas.idea: The toll road on AI compute — 50-DMA held as intraday support June 22 (session low $206.50); June 24 dual catalyst (Annual Meeting + Micron Q3 $34.66B/$19.95 EPS/>80% gross margin) is 48 hours away; the structural accumulation window is the post-FOMC discount at $205–$215.
ideas.why: NVDA's June 22 session (low $206.50, 50-DMA at $206.74, volume 241M vs avg 161.7M) is the technical and institutional confirmation that the June 18 50-DMA recovery was structural. The elevated volume on a 50-DMA-test day is the clearest possible institutional accumulation signal — 241M shares traded while the stock held its long-term moving average. The June 24 compound event (Micron Q3 HBM demand confirmation + Jensen Huang's first post-FOMC public AI capex commentary) is the week's primary conviction anchor. Micron's gross margin expected above 80% on sold-out HBM capacity through 2027 is the structural proof that the AI compute cycle is not peaking — it is accelerating. At $205–$215, NVDA trades at approximately 30x forward earnings (FY27, ~$91B revenue consensus) — the cheapest AI-compute-toll-road entry point since early 2026.
ideas.driver: Hyperscaler + sovereign AI capex compounding through 2028+; Vera Rubin rack-scale systems entering production 2026–2027; HBM4E supply chain execution confirmed (SK Hynix 12-layer, sold-out through 2027); inference demand following training ramp; CUDA ecosystem moat expanding into robotics and physical AI; $299 analyst consensus PT (62 analysts) = +43% from $209.52 intraday estimate.
ideas.risk: Custom ASICs (Google TPU v6, AWS Trainium 3, Meta MTIA 2) erode H100/B200 share in inference workloads faster than expected; Micron Q3 miss on HBM signals AI memory demand cycle peaking before Vera Rubin ramp; Fed delivers 2026 rate hikes creating sustained 30Y above 5.25% that structurally compresses AI-capex multiples.

ideas.name: SK Hynix (000660.KS)
ideas.idea: 12-layer HBM4E samples confirmed; ADR Nasdaq listing July–August 2026 ($66B total shareholder return, $14B ADR raise); HBM shortage extending through 2028; $66B return program confirmed; June 25 KST is the primary Micron read-through gap-up session.
ideas.why: SK Hynix's structural position is strengthening with every new data point from June 22. The Seoul Economic Daily June 22 article confirming the ADR process is proceeding normally (SEC clearance expected late June, share price set only just before debut — standard practice) removes the final ambiguity around process vs. timeline. The $66B total shareholder return program ($14B ADR + buyback — KED Global) is the largest shareholder return commitment in Korean semiconductor history. HBM4E 12-layer samples (48GB, 16Gbps per pin, 20%+ power efficiency vs prior gen) position SK Hynix as the clear HBM4E leader: 58% global market share, NVIDIA supply lock through 2030, shortage extending through 2028. Micron Q3 June 24 (EPS $19.95 est., revenue $34.66B, >80% gross margin, HBM sold-out through 2027) is the structural validation event that resets the global AI memory thesis for all buy-side desks.
ideas.driver: HBM4→4E product transition with SK Hynix as performance leader (58% share, 12-layer confirmed, shortage through 2028); NVIDIA supply lock through 2030; ADR Nasdaq listing July–August 2026 creating structural US demand channel ($66B total return); mandatory sell-side PT revision from ₩2,690,000 to ₩3.0M+; KOSPI 9,000 passive inflow structural bid; ₩75T+ buyback component.
ideas.risk: Samsung executes credible HBM4E capacity ramp with specific NVIDIA qualification before SK Hynix completes customer qualification; ADR SEC clearance delayed materially (reduces near-term demand catalyst); AI capex cycle pauses in 2027 causing memory oversupply before HBM4E shortage fully resolves.

ideas.name: Microsoft
ideas.idea: Lowest-risk path to enterprise AI monetization — post-FOMC dip to ~$378 is the structural accumulation window for the most recurring-revenue-driven megacap; Azure AI workloads compounding regardless of rate path.
ideas.why: Microsoft's enterprise AI thesis compounds on a subscription-revenue model that is structurally rate-insensitive (contracted enterprise bookings at fixed prices for 12–36 months). June 22 developments reinforcing the MSFT long: (1) Micron Q3 sold-out HBM through 2027 is directly positive for Azure AI workload growth expectations — cloud providers are the primary HBM customers; (2) DXY at 100.76 (above 100 still) is the only macro headwind, but MSFT's enterprise contracts are USD-denominated and insulated from FX; (3) The 50-DMA recovery in NVDA on June 22 signals AI capex is accelerating, not declining — Azure is the primary beneficiary of sustained US hyperscaler AI capex. At ~$378 post-FOMC, MSFT is the safest vehicle for investors who want AI monetization exposure without the gate-dependent complexity of NVDA or the stop-clock dynamics of BTC.
ideas.driver: Azure AI workload attach rates compounding; Copilot enterprise adoption across hundreds of millions of seats; OpenAI relationship providing frontier model differentiation and enterprise AI bundle pricing power; subscription model providing rate-insensitive contracted cash flows.
ideas.risk: AI capex-to-Azure-revenue monetization lag extends beyond H2 2026; antitrust scrutiny of OpenAI relationship limits bundling; SPCX's Cursor AI (1M+ developers) creates a new channel through which AI-native developer tooling displaces Microsoft's GitHub Copilot over a 2–4 year horizon.

ideas.name: Alphabet
ideas.idea: Cheapest full-stack AI at the megacap cohort's lowest forward multiple — TPU inference cost advantage; June 24 AI capex confirmation is the secondary catalyst for the entire AI monetization cohort re-rating.
ideas.why: Alphabet owns Gemini (frontier models), TPUs (cost-competitive inference at scale), Google Cloud (enterprise AI inflecting), and search (generating the cash for all of it). At ~$355 post-FOMC selloff, the forward multiple is the lowest in the megacap cohort. Micron's June 24 HBM sold-out confirmation directly validates Google Cloud's AI workload infrastructure investments — a MU beat on HBM demand means Google's hyperscaler AI capex was correctly placed. The TPU cost advantage in inference creates a structural pricing moat for Google Cloud AI workloads against Azure and AWS at higher rates. June 22 data: NVDA's 50-DMA support at $206.74 holding (on 241M volume) is the sector confirmation that AI compute demand is intact — GOOGL is the second-derivative beneficiary.
ideas.driver: TPU-driven inference cost advantage; Gemini integration across billion-user surfaces; Google Cloud AI workload attach rates inflecting; search moat extension (AI Overviews increasing session length per Q1 2026 data); potential search-moat expansion rather than cannibalization.
ideas.risk: DOJ antitrust remedies fracture the search + advertising bundle; AI Overviews prove to be session-length headwind in Q2 2026 data; higher-for-longer rates extend multiple compression before AI Overviews thesis can compound.

ideas.name: SpaceX
ideas.idea: Generational franchise with triple-IG validation (Moody's Baa1, Fitch BBB+, S&P BBB) now being priced in — IG ratings gap-up to ~$185 on June 22; watch for two consecutive closes above $185 to re-engage the 3–5 year thesis at current levels.
ideas.why: SpaceX owns the only proven reusable orbital launch system at scale, Starlink at 5M+ subscribers growing ~40% annually, Starshield national-security contracts, and the Cursor AI coding platform (Anysphere, $60B stock acquisition, 1M+ developer users — not in any IG rating agency assessment). The Moody's Baa1 / Fitch BBB+ / S&P BBB ratings, confirmed within days of the IPO, are permanent franchise-quality anchors. June 22's IG pricing gap-up from $174.90 to ~$185 (+5.77%) is the equity market's first opportunity to agree with what three rating agencies concluded independently. The 3–5 year thesis: Starlink grows to $20B+ annualized revenue; Starship reduces cost-to-orbit by 10–50x creating a new satellite economy; Cursor AI adds a recurring software revenue layer that the IG rating agencies did not factor; all three together at $2.54T market cap = the case for re-rating as the category-defining space infrastructure company.
ideas.driver: Starlink subscriber and ARPU compounding toward $20B+ annualized revenue (currently 5M+ subs at ~$120/mo ARPU); Starship cost-to-orbit structural economics enabling new satellite economy; Cursor AI software revenue layer (1M+ developers, not in IG models); Starshield national-security base load providing government revenue stability; IG ratings permanently lowering cost of capital.
ideas.risk: IPO-cycle overvaluation requires sustained multiple compression before value investors engage; September 2 first earnings disappoints vs $2.54T implied expectations; key-person concentration risk (Elon Musk); December 9 lock-up expiry first major supply event; 84x revenue at $185 remains most extreme US public equity valuation multiple.

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: Double-bottom ($62,255–$62,313) intact through the second stop-clock event; fixed supply × ETF access × halving cycle × DXY structural decline = $75,000–$85,000 Q3-Q4 2026 target; Day 2 stop clock reset probable June 22 UTC.
ideas.why: BTC's structural framework is proving its design: the two-consecutive-close stop rule has now survived two separate Day 1 events (June 18 FOMC dump at $62,953 and June 21 stop-hunt at $63,313) without the double-bottom ($62,255–$62,313) being breached. June 22 UTC current price ($64,117) is $617 above the $63,500 stop — reset probability is high. The long-term thesis: fixed supply (21M BTC hard cap) × widening institutional access (IBIT AUM $94B+ post-outflow) × halving cycle supply reduction (April 2024) × DXY structural decline (Hormuz → oil lower → CPI relief → rate pivot) = $75,000–$85,000 Q3-Q4 2026. BTC's multi-year thesis runs on halvings and institutional access, not FOMC meetings. The DXY at 100.76 (above 100 gate) is the single remaining macro headwind — when DXY clears 100, the structural BTC rally resumes.
ideas.driver: Fixed supply meeting widening institutional access (ETFs at $94B+ AUM, corporate treasuries); DXY structural decline as Hormuz reopening removes the oil-inflation driver that anchored dollar strength; IBIT inflows restarting signals institutional accumulation beginning; halving cycle supply reduction (April 2024) creating structural supply deficit; 'digital gold' narrative in Warsh 'no forward guidance' regime.
ideas.risk: Warsh delivers multiple 2026 rate hikes (sustained DXY above 103 is structurally bearish for BTC over 6–12 months); IBIT outflow resumption proves June 12 single-session inflow was one-off; two Day 1 events in the same recovery cycle suggests structural demand at $63,500–$64,500 is thinner than expected.

ideas.name: Amazon
ideas.idea: AWS AI infrastructure + Hormuz logistics tailwind — post-FOMC dip to ~$183 is the best megacap cloud entry; Micron Q3 June 24 is the direct AWS AI capex validation event.
ideas.why: Amazon runs the world's largest commercial cloud (AWS), is ramping Trainium/Inferentia custom silicon to reduce AI inference costs, and has the logistics-Prime flywheel that scales into robotic AI. Micron Q3's sold-out HBM capacity through 2027 is a direct AWS AI workload growth signal — AWS is one of Micron's primary HBM customers. If MU beats on June 24 and confirms AI memory demand through 2027, it directly validates AWS AI revenue growth expectations for H2 2026 and 2027. The Iran ceasefire (Hormuz reopening on 30-day mine-clearance timeline) is an Amazon-specific logistics tailwind: shipping cost inflation decreases as Hormuz commercial traffic normalizes, improving Prime delivery margins and fulfillment economics by an estimated 5–10%. June 22 data: SPX at 7,487–7,500 (above 7,460 gate floor) and NVDA 50-DMA holding (241M institutional volume) are the broad market and sector signals that confirm the accumulation thesis.
ideas.driver: AWS AI workload attach rates + Trainium/Inferentia inference cost advantage; Prime and logistics flywheel compounding at scale; Hormuz reopening reducing shipping cost inflation 5–10%; AI-native robotics expansion in fulfillment centers creating operational leverage; Micron June 24 AWS AI capex validation.
ideas.risk: Cloud spending deceleration if enterprise IT budgets tighten in higher-rate environment; competitive pressure from Azure and Google Cloud on enterprise AI workload share; Trainium/Inferentia ramp timelines extending beyond 2027; logistics cost inflation reversing Hormuz-reopening gains.
